conceptual assets.information: The 32-bit word written by the bus and serialized as NeoLED output data; the LED engine depends on it to emit the requested payload.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus data is loaded into the transmit word at line 192 and then shifted and emitted through the serial engine at lines 239, 257 and 318. Availability is at risk because disabling the unit clears the transmit buffer at line 193 and the engine's state is controlled by enable at line 231, which can discard or withhold the payload.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could inject or corrupt bus write data, or disable the unit so queued payload data is cleared and never transmitted.

conceptual assets.concept: LED transfer format and strobe controls
conceptual assets.information: The mode and strobe settings determine how each queued word is interpreted and which serial operation follows it; the LED transmission behavior depends on these controls.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus writes modify the mode and strobe settings at lines 131 and 132, and those values select the active word format and subsequent state at lines 240 and 248.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could rewrite the mode or strobe control bits so the emitted LED transaction uses the wrong format or operation.

conceptual assets.information: The clock prescaler and total, zero-bit, and one-bit timing values determine the rate and pulse widths of NeoLED transmission; correct LED signaling depends on these settings.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus writes store the timing settings at lines 133 and 135 through 137, after which they control clock selection and pulse timing at lines 225, 261, 263 and 285. Availability is at risk because those settings control the clocked progress and timing of the serial output, so altered values can stall or withhold transmission at lines 225 and 285.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write extreme or incompatible prescaler and timing values to corrupt the waveform or prevent the serial engine from completing a transfer.

conceptual assets.information: The enable setting controls whether the clock generator is enabled, whether the transmit buffer is cleared, and whether serial operation can run; the IP depends on it to operate.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a bus write changes the enable setting at line 130, which controls multiple operational paths. Availability is at risk because the setting drives the clock-enable output at line 160, clears the transmit buffer when deasserted at line 193, and controls serial state at line 231.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could clear the enable setting, disabling the clock output and clearing queued LED data so the IP stops transmitting.

conceptual assets.information: The interrupt configuration selects whether the interrupt is based on an empty or half-full transmit buffer; interrupt behavior depends on this threshold policy.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the threshold configuration is written from bus data at line 134 and selects the interrupt condition at lines 202 and 203. Availability is at risk because changing this setting can suppress or delay the interrupt needed to service the transmit buffer at lines 202 and 203.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could rewrite the threshold configuration so the service interrupt is asserted at the wrong occupancy level or is withheld.

conceptual assets.information: The interrupt notification reports that the transmit buffer has reached the configured service condition; an integrating controller may depend on it to refill or service the LED transmitter. It is generated internally and has no entry port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because irq_o is produced from enable, threshold configuration and buffer occupancy at lines 201 through 203, allowing the notification to be forged or suppressed. Availability is at risk because withholding irq_o can prevent the controller from servicing the transmit buffer and can block continued operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the enable, threshold, or buffer state so irq_o is falsely asserted or withheld and the transmitter is not serviced.
